text:
maria: Quick follow-up to the CP handshake RFC — noticed a pattern during private VPC onboards where cert fetch/rotation traffic spikes and causes 5-15s attach latency for a subset of customers. Can we discuss observability and a low-risk batching/attestation path?

kevin: Yep saw that in staging last night. The stack traces show we do a KMS cert fetch per connector attach serially. If 50 connectors attach in parallel you get N concurrent KMS ops.

anita: That matches the audit logs I inspected. Problem: if we batch at the CP level we might obscure tenant-level attestation events that compliance teams rely on. Need to preserve per-tenant auditability.

maria: Agreed. Here's a short log sample from the spike:
[2026-02-18T03:12:01Z] attach.start tenant=acme-corp conn=connector-23
[2026-02-18T03:12:01Z] cert.fetch.start fetch_id=F-9a3
[2026-02-18T03:12:03Z] cert.fetch.end fetch_id=F-9a3 duration=1.8s
[2026-02-18T03:12:03Z] attach.end tenant=acme-corp conn=connector-23 duration=2.1s

tom: One idea: move KMS-bound cert fetch to the control plane only and have CP mint a short-lived per-tenant attach token (signed by CP cert). Connectors present the token to CP gateway; CP validates (no KMS hit), emits tenant-level audit, then returns an ephemeral session credential. Flow (very rough):

  connector -> CP auth endpoint (present tenant identity)
  CP -> KMS (once per region or intermittent) to obtain/renew CP cert
  CP -> mint signed token (per-attach, TTL 1m) -> connector
  connector -> attach using token -> CP validates and returns session creds

anita: That preserves tenant audit because CP still logs the token mint event with tenant metadata. Good. Concerns: CP becomes a certificate/attestation hotspot and could increase blast radius.

kevin: We can mitigate hotspot risk by: (1) regional CP replicas, (2) token minting rate limiting, (3) short token TTL + replay protection. Also add circuit-breakers so heavy attach bursts get queued and connectors see a clear retry header.

maria: From an observability POV, we should add: histogram of attach_latency, counter cert_fetch_count, gauge token_cache_hit_rate, and an "attach_reason" tag (onboard / reconnect / failover). Example metrics query for Grafana:

histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(attach_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, region))
rate(cert_fetch_count[1m]) by (region)

judy: I'll wire up dashboards and an alert if 95th attach latency > 3s for >5m. Also add a panel for token cache hit rate and a table for recent failed attaches (with tenant and error).

sre-bot: deploy: canary rollout scheduled: 2026-04-01T02:00:00Z -> 2026-04-01T04:00:00Z. Link: https://ci.internal/release/attach-token-spike (canary target: 10% region traffic).

anita: One more ops note: on private/on-prem installs connectors may not reach CP (e.g., isolated customer networks). We need a graceful local fallback: connectors should maintain a small local cert cache and use exponential backoff; CP should accept cached proofs briefly and surface a drift alert.

tom: Action summary: (1) implement CP token signing service + regional replicas (KEVIN owns replication plan), (2) add cache TTL config + token replay protection (TOM owns token service), (3) add metrics + dashboard (JUDY), (4) on-prem fallback and drift alert (ANITA). I'll pick up the initial spike implementation and a small compatibility shim. :thumbsup:

kevin: ack. Rough estimate: spike + telemetry in 1 sprint, replication + hardening in 2 sprints.

maria: Sounds good — let's keep the canary conservative. TOM, please post a short design doc link when you have the token service sketch so SRE can validate failure modes.

tom: Will do, I’ll drop a short doc tomorrow with sequence diagrams and a failure-mode table.

judy: Added the dashboard ticket to the infra board (INFRA-834).

sre-bot: note: monitoring policy update required: attach_latency alert added to staging only (will be promoted with canary success).

maria: Thanks all — this should reduce the KMS storm and give better telemetry while keeping tenant-level audit. If anyone sees corner cases ping me directly.

kevin: closing loop: also consider a rate-limited pre-warm path for expected bulk onboards (e.g., customer migration flows) so we can pre-cache tokens without hammering KMS.

anita: Good call — add a prewarm API with explicit operator intent and a one-time audit event.

maria: +1. We'll incorporate in the rollout playbook. :white_check_mark:
